note: Re-judged 2026-11-02 by an independent auditor who authored none of the changes named. RFC 7999 Section 4: "Without an explicit configuration directive set by the operator, network elements SHOULD NOT discard traffic destined towards IP prefixes that are tagged with the BLACKHOLE community." ab9d8ce252 moved both filter_modify units from handleFilterUpdate text to the live entry evaluateModify (registered by p.OnFilter in filter_modify.go) over the engine's fields object, the community written by Community(0xffff029a).String() as the event formatter writes it. Positive: a modify matching only 65001:100 must answer accept with no Sets and no Update for the 65535:666 route, so the announced next hop stays and nothing is discarded. Negative (directive present): a modify matching blackhole must answer modify with exactly next-hop set "192.0.2.1". Same inputs, assertions now on the Sets the chain resolves, which is what reaches the wire; a filter that rewrote regardless of directive fails the positive, one that never rewrote fails the negative. RIB units byte-identical. Verdict unchanged: enforced.
